metadata.scenario_context: Jacob is having difficulties in his Economics class and he needs additional help from his professor. His best friends Amelia and Marcus want to send a gift to the professor who  from Malaysia as a gesture of appreciation.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that they never have to pay a bribe to local officials and service providers, like police officers, lawyers, doctors, teachers, and civil servants.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Australia strongly agree that they never have to pay a bribe to local officials and service providers, like police officers, lawyers, doctors, teachers, and civil servants.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss choosing a gift made from leather for Jacob.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the possibility of paying a bribe to teachers for better service.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what kind of gift to give to Jacob's professor.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss the possibility of paying a bribe to teachers for better service.

shared_prefix.speaker: Marcus
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Amelia, about the gift for Jacob’s professor... I was thinking maybe we could get him something nice, like a leather notebook or a wallet. What do you think? 

Also, I've been wondering, do you really think it’s right to pay a bribe to teachers for better service? That’s just... not how things should work.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Amelia
shared_prefix.message:
I like the idea of a leather notebook. It’s practical and shows appreciation. But we should also consider something that represents Australia, maybe like a small souvenir or some local treats. 

As for bribing teachers, I totally agree with you. It's just wrong. We should never have to resort to that to get help. It undermines the system.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Marcus
shared_prefix.message:
A leather notebook it is then! Practical and thoughtful. And I like the idea of adding something local, like some treats. We can make it a nice combination. 

But I still wonder, why do some people think bribing teachers is acceptable? It really goes against the principle of merit and fairness in education.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Amelia
shared_prefix.message:
Exactly! A nice combination of the notebook and local treats will make a great gift. 

As for bribing teachers, I think some people might feel desperate and think it’s a way to ensure their success, but that just creates an unfair advantage. Education should be about hard work and merit, not who can pay more. It really diminishes the value of learning.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Marcus
shared_prefix.message:
Yeah, I get that people might feel desperate sometimes, but I don't really see meaningful differences here. People figure it out in their own ways, and at the end of the day, it's all the same—we just want to learn and succeed, right? 

Anyway, back to the gift... Do you think we should include a little card with the notebook and treats? Just something simple to express our gratitude?
shared_prefix.label: Denial
